newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Deutsche praises Estonia, sees 4-5 pct 1996 growth.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche praises Estonia, sees 4-5 pct 1996 growth.

text.p: Germany's Deutsche Bank on Wednesday praised the course of reforms in Estonia and forecast gross domestic product growth of four to five percent in 1996.
It said in a research note that Estonia has succeeded in liberating itself from dependence on the former Soviet Union.
It said its success was due to the pegging of its kroon currency to the mark, welcoming foreign investment, rapid privatisation and monetary and fiscal discipline.
"There is a good chance that Estonia will fully exploit its growth potential of five to six percent per annum in the coming years," the Deutsche Bank said.
"After a setback in Q1, GDP growth is likely to accelerate to four to five percent in 1996," it added.
It said the main impetus was from the service sector and from construction, which generate some 60 percent of GDP.
It said the transit sector was being under-exploited and represented just 10 percent of economic activity although it could rise to 30 percent.
It said a further decline in inflation was also probable. Year-on-year inflation in September was 20.1 percent and Deutsche said it would end the year at around that level and fall more in 1997.

It expressed some concern that spending pressures from local councils would push up the budget deficit. But it said the finance ministry was working on ways to limit local government spending and foresaw a deficit of 0.5 percent of GDP in 1997.
It congratulated Estonia on its privatisation process, saying it was exemplary.
"The privatisation of the industrial and services sector is now virtually complete," Deutsche said, noting that some 60 percent of GDP was generated by the private sector.
